newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr slips in Tokyo on LDP official's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Dlr slips in Tokyo on LDP official's remarks.

text.p: 0435 GMT --*Dollar eased slightly in early afternoon Tokyo trade after reported remarks by key ruling party official Taku Yamasaki pushed down Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

*Yamasaki, chairman of the LDP policy research council, was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying the option of implementing fiscal stimulus steps such as an extra budget will not be ruled out in government's planned fiscal reform law.
*Dollar supported by solid bids below 115.90 yen.
*"A big fall in dollar/yen is unlikely as exporters are in no great hurry to sell," a city bank trader said.
*Short-covering interest in mark/yen from interbank players seen around 67.10 yen, dealers said.
*Mark/yen could test lower when short-covering activity near 67 yen is out of the way, dealers said.

0300 GMT - *Dollar flat against yen by midday Tokyo on Thursday after earlier dipping on mark/yen sales. It steadied against mark after earlier attempt to trigger stop-loss sales below 1.7250 marks failed.
*Despite lingering uncertainty over European single currency, trading was subdued since operators in Tokyo lacked energy to pile up further mark short positions.
*Dollar tried to test downside against mark in early trade after failing to rise above resistance of 1.7330 marks overnight.

*"Although a dispute between the Bundesbank and the Bonn government over plans to revalue Germany's gold reserves has been resolved, there is still uncertainty over the EMU," said a senior dealer at a European bank. "There will still be many operators willing to sell marks below 1.72," he added.
*But a dealer at a Japanese bank said that since many operators had already taken heavy mark short positions, there were few incentives for them to pile up more.
